name: Dinosaur National Monument
story: Dinosaur National Monument covers 210,844 acres in Colorado and Utah, encompassing the river canyons of the Green and Yampa. It was proclaimed a national monument in 1915 to protect its famous Dinosaur Quarry and contains over 800 paleontological sites with dinosaur fossils.
matters: The park preserves a wealth of natural history, including rock layers from the Jurassic Period containing ancient animal remains and sites used by the prehistoric Fremont culture.
